policies.title: Bahrain: named online-eligible ordinary passports with eVisa route
policies.summary: For these previously unsupported passport rows whose snapshot already records eVisa, NPRA's live country list names the country as online-eligible and its process page confirms an NPRA-reviewed online visa issuance workflow.
conditions: This policy is confined to ordinary-passport rows that were previously unsupported and already normalized as eVisa in the snapshot. The live online list names the corresponding countries, but says terms and conditions apply and directs a traveller to country-specific eligibility; it does not establish an unconditional exemption or a special-passport rule.

The portal describes a genuine pre-travel electronic-visa workflow: the traveller completes the online eligibility and application flow, uploads documents, pays, undergoes NPRA processing, and receives approval notification. It is not merely an arrival-registration form.

Passport validity, funds, accommodation, return/onward travel, sponsor, prior-document, residence, GCC-status, profession, purpose, fee, duration, entry-count, security, sanctions, and final-admission conditions remain traveller- and visa-type-specific. They were not exposed as a reproducible code-level crosswalk in this review.

The separately promoted GCC-citizenship exemption, Bahrain citizenship, GCC-resident eVisa, family, work, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, UN, emergency, refugee, and other special-document routes are not classified by this policy. Border officers retain final admission authority.

application.label: Bahrain NPRA eVisa service
steps: Use the official service's eligibility flow and select the applicable visa type and conditions.
Complete the online application, upload the required documents, and pay the required application fee.
Await NPRA review and approval before travel; present the issued visa and any required entry documents for border examination.

policies.title: Bahrain: Iran, North Korea, and Kosovo ordinary passports requiring advance visa
policies.summary: Iran, North Korea, and Kosovo are not named in either live NPRA online or on-arrival country schedule. Bahrain's National Portal expressly gives the residual rule that a non-on-arrival country needs an entry visa issued in advance through an embassy, sponsor, or travel agency.
conditions: This is the National Portal's explicit advance-issuance residual for nationalities outside the on-arrival schedule, read with the current online and on-arrival country schedules. It is not inferred from a commercial passport index or from a failed application.

The cited schedules do not name these three catalog passport codes. The National Portal describes advance issuance through a Bahrain embassy in the country of residence, a Bahraini sponsor, or a travel agency; it does not establish a nationality-wide self-service eVisa route for them.

This policy does not decide any resident-, GCC-status-, third-country-document-, invitation-, work-, residence-, transit-, diplomatic-, official-, service-, refugee-, emergency-, or special-document exception. Visa issuance, security screening, sanctions, carrier checks, and final admission remain applicable.

conflicts.officialStatus: entry visa required; eVisa and on-arrival routes both named but exact ordinary-passport route is not established
conflicts.explanation: Ukraine is not one of the five GCC citizenships exempted by the National Portal. Both live NPRA schedules name Ukraine, but their country-specific terms are not exposed and conflict with the National Portal's 69-country and NPRA's 68-country arrival counts; the visa_free fallback is contradicted but no single normalized replacement is safe.
